- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward trend after a recent spike, it often overestimates; cap forecast growth at 0.5–1% per day after peak.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 0.3–0.7% per day.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model is flat or rising, it’s likely overconfident; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is consistently below 80 and true outcome rises above 82, it’s a “lag error” — model is too slow to react; add 0.2–0.8% to forecast for next 2–3 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of 2–3 prior days to anchor forecast.
